title: 8 heads (HEAD_DIM 64) + 2^18 batch at device batch 128
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (n_head 4->8 at identical params/FLOPs/VRAM) combined with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17->2**18 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64->128 (grad_accum stays 1).
reflection: val_bpb 0.993168; 1810 steps, 474.5M tokens, steady-state MFU 37.99%, peak VRAM 45.0GB. The throughput half of the change did exactly what a1/a2 predicted: device batch 128 restored MFU to ~38% (per-step log sits at 39-40%) and bought 474.5M tokens vs ~420M for every device-batch-64 run, i.e. +13% tokens. Head count is confirmed throughput-neutral: 8 heads at head_dim 64 ran at the same MFU as 4 heads at 128, same params (50.3M), and VRAM is set by the device batch (45GB, same region as the original 2^19/128 baseline). What I CANNOT claim is the head-count effect on quality: I deliberately confounded it with the batch change so that the plain (2^18,128) run from a1/a2 serves as the control, and the head_dim delta is their number minus mine. Against round 0's token regression (-0.000097 bpb per 1M tokens, fitted on identical code) 474.5M tokens alone predicts ~0.991, so my 0.993168 is if anything slightly on the wrong side of that line -- but that regression was fitted across a cold-GPU outlier and has no business resolving 0.002. Bottom line honest read: 0.993168 is inside the 0.0019-sd replication band of the current baseline 0.992664, so this run does not by itself demonstrate an improvement over it; what it does establish firmly is that (2^18, device batch 128) recovers the lost 13% of tokens, and that 8 heads costs nothing to run.
